title: Issued full-review permits with a department missing from the record
question: How many permits issued after in-house review have no Planning, building or Fire review step on record?
finding: Of 9,451 permits issued 2020 to 2026 after in-house review that have review rows, additions alterations or repairs: 6,970 issued, 1,235 with no Planning step (18%), 9 with no Building Inspection step, 3,160 with no Fire step; type 9 (no name in the table; most descriptions begin “solar permit:”): 440 issued, 440 with no Planning step (100%), 0 with no Building Inspection step, 0 with no Fire step; demolitions: 374 issued, 25 with no Planning step (7%), 0 with no Building Inspection step, 275 with no Fire step.
how: Permits marked In-House in the issuance table (original application, addendum 0, not fire-only), against the departments that appear in their review rows.
limits: Not every job needs every department: interior work with no change of use may need no Planning review, and work with no life-safety element may need no Fire review. Which departments the law requires for which work depends on the codes and departmental routing rules; the code text confirms routing for site permits (Building Code 106A.3.4.2) but not a fixed list for every alteration. A missing row may be a data gap rather than a skipped step.
